subject.title: fix(markdown-core): guard against NaN in ordered list start attribute

question: Should markdown-core defensively support non-numeric ordered-list token attributes, or must this PR first demonstrate an actual supported caller or extension path that can produce one?
rationale: The code guard is plausible, but the public conversion path and new tests do not establish that the malformed token can reach this renderer; repository intent is needed after actual-path evidence is supplied.

options.title: Require actual-path evidence
options.body: Ask for a malformed-token regression test and redacted before/after renderer output before deciding whether to merge the guard.

options.title: Accept defensive hardening
options.body: Merge the low-cost guard despite the currently unproven caller path, while requiring a test that directly exercises the branch.

options.title: Decline unreachable hardening
options.body: Close the PR if markdown-core only accepts parser-produced tokens and no supported extension path can mutate the start attribute.

recommendation.title: Require actual-path evidence
recommendation.body: Ask for a malformed-token regression test and redacted before/after renderer output before deciding whether to merge the guard.
